<span id="paper-foundation-models-alps-4489dea8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3824083e7eb834df">Why does ALPS want one visual representation for language, state prediction, and image inspection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Planning needs predictability, instruction tasks need language alignment, and inspection needs readable image recovery. Shared patch tokens support those interfaces, but each must be tested. Pixel reconstruction alone does not establish planning, nor language alignment complete physical state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A robot needs to understand “move the cup right,” predict its location, and inspect the future image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3824083e7eb834df">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:alps" data-paper-title="ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d4c87309e5eec26">Why supervise only teacher-crop B patches that fall inside student crop A in stage two?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The student sees only A, so exact targets outside A would supervise invisible content. Map geometry first, then predict frozen teacher targets at corresponding positions; appearance augmentation promotes robustness. Shared initialization does not mean the teacher updates with the student.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If the student sees the left half, supervise only the overlap, not small text on the unseen right.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d4c87309e5eec26">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:alps" data-paper-title="ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f22083ac5b1aebb">How does the fixed stage-one teacher differ from an EMA teacher?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Stage one initializes the student and a teacher frozen through stage two. EMA would move targets with student weights, which is a different method. Training drops the cross-view predictor afterward and deploys the student encoder and language interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Student augmentation training may change the encoder while fixed clean-crop teacher targets remain unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f22083ac5b1aebb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:alps" data-paper-title="ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f9c95b863618d1a">Why average the cross-crop loss over valid patches per image before averaging the batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aalps">ALPS: Visual State Encoders for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Cruz</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Overlap sizes differ; per-image means prevent large overlaps dominating. A B patch is valid if its center falls in A&#x27;s half-open bounds. Empty overlap safely contributes zero, while the sampler separately enforces a minimum valid count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With 100 matching patches in one image and ten in another, a flat token mean gives tenfold weight to the first; image means do not.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 验证与结果边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30120v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30120-alps/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f9c95b863618d1a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:aw0" data-paper-title="Agentic World Action Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-aw0-c41ecc38" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-63a711c06d27630b">Why combine composable programs, future vision, and robot action in one AW-0 model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aaw0">Agentic World Action Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Programs provide reusable steps, video anticipates scenes, and continuous actions control the robot. Three experts jointly link plan to physical consequences; generated code plans by default rather than being executed. Local work reviews evidence only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate “grasp then place,” forecast the scene, and produce controls without running arbitrary Python.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30136v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.30136-aw0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-63a711c06d27630b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:aw0" data-paper-title="Agentic World Action Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b0c5a8e2785d041b">Why allow bidirectionality within AW-0 experts but enforce code→video→action across them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aaw0">Agentic World Action Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bidirectionality organizes representations inside a modality; block causality preserves conditioning from plan to scene prediction to control. Code must not see later videos or actions, while action can use earlier code and predicted scenes. Full mutual visibility changes inference order and available information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate a cup-grasp program, predict the scene, then output controls; do not give the planner future ground-truth actions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30136v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.30136-aw0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b0c5a8e2785d041b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:aw0" data-paper-title="Agentic World Action Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-80ec646f7634554a">How do separate expert projections, normalization, and FFNs differ from fully shared transforms?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aaw0">Agentic World Action Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate transforms serve code, video, and action while joint attention exchanges information at prescribed boundaries. They add parameters and interfaces, not guaranteed improvement. The paper combines bidirectional intra-expert and block-causal cross-expert attention.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Discrete code and continuous actions can use separate FFNs and still interact, without being isolated or freely bidirectional.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30136v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.30136-aw0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80ec646f7634554a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:aw0" data-paper-title="Agentic World Action Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-09ecab1ee5f08245">Can flow targets and masked code diffusion use one noise and supervision mask?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Aaw0">Agentic World Action Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC Berkeley</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Video and action use continuous noising and velocity regression. Code uses an independent Bernoulli mask and loss only on masked program tokens. Action noise and code masking are not determined by video noise. Mixed video sampling also needs separate clipped and normalized importance weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Low video noise does not imply lightly masked code; one shared mask changes the paper&#x27;s independent sampling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地收录与复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30136v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.30136-aw0/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-09ecab1ee5f08245">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-dt-jepa-898e3cdc" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-656e6bff07c6b2fa">Why might a Decision Transformer need more than expected return?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equal returns can lead to different states, so one return-to-go cannot distinguish dynamics. DT-JEPA conditions actions on a predicted future representation distribution from history, not an observed future. Manage uncertainty and isolate training-only inputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Routes with equal reward may reach a charger or an exit; state predictions provide information absent from the scalar.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-656e6bff07c6b2fa">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-07079ed5e9b5243c">Why predict future latents from history and expose true future only to the training target encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The future is unavailable at decision time, so reading it would leak. History predicts a distribution and reparameterized samples condition decisions. The EMA target only supplies training alignment. Future representations distinguish dynamics even at equal return.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two trajectories can score ten, yet one hits an obstacle and the other stays clear.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-07079ed5e9b5243c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4edbb4e720f6808c">What is the trade-off between a Gaussian future distribution and a deterministic vector?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Mean and variance express uncertainty; reparameterized samples condition DT. A deterministic vector is a single point. The diagonal Gaussian is still limited and does not cover arbitrary multimodality or allow real future input at deployment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Variance can represent uncertainty between routes, but a single Gaussian may not capture two distant discrete destinations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4edbb4e720f6808c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:dt-jepa" data-paper-title="DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-92f993e968b93b89">Can NLL, BC, and critic reductions all use generic MSE.mean?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adt-jepa">DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Southeast University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Sum NLL over latent dimensions before the batch mean; sum BC and critic over time and action dimensions before the batch mean. Reductions change relative weights. Detach target and TD bootstrap, but retain actor gradients through Q with respect to actions. Local tests omit full online data collection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling action width changes an all-element mean&#x27;s per-example contribution relative to other summed terms.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32657v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.32657-dt-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-92f993e968b93b89">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ego-p2c-b2c2eae5" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-47077d41b441deb0">Why improve both question planning and perceptual answers in egocentric spatial reasoning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complex questions need decisions about where to look and what to ask, followed by reliable evidence extraction. Errors in either role propagate. EgoP²C improves both while respecting their information boundaries; final conclusions still need validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For a drawer relative to a door, plan a viewpoint and subquestion; a left/right perceptual error cannot be fixed by fluent composition.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与信息边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-47077d41b441deb0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c60c2b24dcf80f55">Why must role teachers score the same student tokens in segmented distillation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Actual student interaction defines visited prefixes. Role-specific teachers score those prefixes to identify planning, perception, or direct-answer errors. A separate teacher-written answer loses on-policy supervision. Shared video KV must exclude role-private history.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If a student asks for a viewpoint then makes a spatial judgment, teachers score the corresponding segments of that same trace.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与信息边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c60c2b24dcf80f55">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2509c24f0c7580c">Do the PC, V, and general G experts share the same parameter training boundaries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Experts initialize from copies of the base FFN. G&#x27;s FFN stays frozen, while its attention residual trains only in MOPD. PC and V supply trainable planning and perception paths. This preserves general answering without updating three full models alike.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keeping G&#x27;s FFN does not forbid all adaptation; its attention residual can train later.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与信息边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2509c24f0c7580c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ego-p2c" data-paper-title="EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a6f0616beea54a27">Why normalize role length over the whole trajectory?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aego-p2c">EgoP²C: Internalizing Plan-Perceive-Compose for Spatial Reasoning in Egocentric Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Arizona State University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A role may have multiple segments; divide by all supervised tokens for that role in the trajectory, not each segment separately. Otherwise splitting a segment increases role weight. Detach teacher and old-student log probabilities, keep private decoder KV separate, and do not interpret random-teacher diagnostics as spatial capability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten PC tokens in two five-token segments should keep the same total weight. Separate means would double their contribution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与信息边界, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22681">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22681-ego-p2c/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a6f0616beea54a27">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-egojepa-867ae28c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-eace4b99f19a0163">Why learn from human egocentric videos for transferable robot experience?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Robot demonstrations are costly and embodiment-specific. Human video has action–appearance relationships but not robot control signals. Learn latent visual and action structure before adapting to a robot; actual control still needs environment validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Human drawer-opening video teaches scene change, not direct robot-arm joint commands.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eace4b99f19a0163">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-245e1f402013e420">Why learn latent actions instead of mapping human hand trajectories directly to robot joints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Human hands and robot actuators have different geometry. Motion-difference conditioning learns latent actions linked to visual changes, then joint modeling and robot-specific interfaces adapt them. What transfers is the effect, not coordinate equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Fingers pinching and a gripper closing have different angles but can both lift a cup.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-245e1f402013e420">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0417ac0042303b">How do action-conditioned JEPA and later joint visual/latent-action flow matching differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First predict future visual representations conditioned on hand-motion differences, linking latent actions to observable effects. Then jointly model visual and action latents and adapt a robot I/O interface. Prediction and joint generation are separate and do not by themselves establish robot control.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learn which hand changes produce which visual effects before adapting the learned joint structure to an arm.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0417ac0042303b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:egojepa" data-paper-title="EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d9385b48d4f63672">How does visibility of future visual targets differ between JEPA training and control?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aegojepa">EgoJEPA: Beyond Retargeting for Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Videos</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In training, an encoder supplies detached targets from future frames for prediction from history and hand-motion differences. Control cannot read an unrealized future. Local work is a literature/cost record with no adapter, metrics, or GPU receipt.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use the later object-position frame to supervise prediction, not as a deployment input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20904">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.20904-egojepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d9385b48d4f63672">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-esc-e793a8c8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9fcdef57f9d4db58">Why does ESC care whether objects persist across generated viewpoints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generators can render plausible posed images while adding or dropping objects. ESC links RGB and depth to test geometric consistency. New views should differ in pixels in spatially explainable ways, not merely look similar or good.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cup should move in projection as the camera circles a table, not vanish in an unoccluded region.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9fcdef57f9d4db58">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-fdc0872eefd4d85b">Why can a sharp image with the right camera pose still fail PCC?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Realistic appearance does not ensure the same 3D scene. PCC uses bidirectional depth reprojection and visibility to detect vanished or hallucinated objects, respecting occlusion and invalid pixels. Best-of-N selects geometric consistency, not the prettiest candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A cup can disappear in a visually clean view; bidirectional reprojection detects the inconsistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fdc0872eefd4d85b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-da2aafe8b40641a0">How does PCC Best-of-N differ from selecting the closest RGB image?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Correct viewpoints can change pixels. PCC projects source and target depths both ways with occlusion and valid coverage checks, detects missing or hallucinated geometry, and minimizes the score. This does not optimize every image-quality metric.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A duplicate source image can have the smallest RGB difference while failing the requested camera view.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-da2aafe8b40641a0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:esc" data-paper-title="ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-80733d2366c21114">Why do reprojection checks need z-buffering and valid-pixel masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aesc">ESC: Escaping 2D Diffusion Ambiguity with Geometric Constraints for Consistent Novel View Synthesis</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · FAIR at Meta / Mila - Québec AI Institute / Université de Montréal</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Multiple source points can land on one pixel and must respect occlusion. Negative depth, out-of-bounds projections, and missing source depth are not valid errors. PCC also uses thresholds, logarithmic compression, clipping, and coverage normalization. No local implementation or capability metrics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A wall can correctly occlude an object. Lack of a visible match is not disappearance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23732v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23732-esc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-80733d2366c21114">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ev-jepa-12c252ce" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-fd62dd8be67749b5">Why support phone, server, and split-device budgets for one video model?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A fixed width may not fit all devices. Separate models may use incompatible representations. EV-JEPA learns shared elastic widths and compatible handoffs, but not every split is valid or free. Transfer, compression, and task quality need testing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Matching tensor shapes is not enough for a phone&#x27;s narrow front half to hand off to a wide server back half.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fd62dd8be67749b5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-339f1d60618048c6">Why train narrow-to-wide as well as narrow and wide paths?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Individually strong widths need not exchange intermediate states successfully. The mixed route trains the widening boundary under a common frozen teacher. This differs from arbitrary slicing or splicing independent models and does not eliminate communication cost.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A server&#x27;s wide layers may not understand a phone&#x27;s narrow intermediate state without handoff training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-339f1d60618048c6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a740fcbaa2cbbe9d">How does a learned split-layer compressor differ from dropping tokens?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dropping tokens may permanently hide evidence. A compressor trains reconstruction so transmitted representations remain useful to the second stage. Lower reconstruction loss is not end-to-end losslessness or proof of deployed handoff.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Dropping half the spatial positions differs from encoding into fewer tokens and learning to reconstruct recoverable structure.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a740fcbaa2cbbe9d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ev-jepa" data-paper-title="EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5a736aec4cf8931e">Does EV-JEPA&#x27;s teacher stay frozen or track the elastic student by EMA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aev-jepa">EV-JEPA: Elastic V-JEPA for Any Device and Cross-Device Inference</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta Reality Labs Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Frozen V-JEPA 2 supplies common targets for narrow, wide, and mixed student paths. Nested student parameters share masked-token L1 supervision in one space. Channel slicing alone is not joint training or cross-device verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Updating shared student weights leaves the teacher&#x27;s outputs fixed, not updated through EMA.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 边界与后续触发条件. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14324">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.14324-ev-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5a736aec4cf8931e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gen4p-e9a640f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-e01e783591ec19da">Why reuse video generation knowledge for 3D and 4D perception?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Generation pretraining can learn appearance, motion, and geometry priors relevant to depth, tracks, and cameras. Gen4P extracts a clean-video scene representation and queries properties. It still needs geometry targets or task validation, not new video generation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Given a moving-camera clip, query a point&#x27;s 3D trajectory instead of asking for another clip.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e01e783591ec19da">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-e6914c7043932711">Why can a video generator support 4D perception without multistep denoising?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Gen4P reads motion and geometry representations inside a pretrained DiT. Clean video latents get one prescribed conditioned encoding; queries read tracks or depth. Frozen geometry adapters and trainable task LoRA differ. Supervision and decoders remain necessary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train a head to query a point&#x27;s 3D location after three seconds without generating another video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e6914c7043932711">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f62c7e64e5b82850">How do frozen depth-LoRA and trainable 4D-LoRA differ from full fine-tuning?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze the base DiT and depth LoRA; train the 4D LoRA, queries, and decoders. This preserves generation and depth priors more directly than updating all weights. It does not guarantee every metric improves; the paper reports a depth regression.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train a temporal tracking adapter without modifying the depth update, then test both tasks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f62c7e64e5b82850">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gen4p" data-paper-title="Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-15ae281ad1d75986">What distinctions matter for continuous time queries and DiT input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agen4p">Gen4P: Video Generators are 4D Perceivers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Query time interpolates endpoint embeddings with t/(T−1). DiT reads clean z0 under the final scheduler time and an empty text condition. Query time is not diffusion noise time, and this is not iterative denoising. Local work is documentation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A midpoint time query interpolates embeddings; it does not add half-strength noise to the frame.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22371">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22371-gen4p/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-15ae281ad1d75986">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:inside-jepa" data-paper-title="Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-inside-jepa-840eadf0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c81bf3ff739be368">Why does Inside-JEPA want latent states to encode relationships?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainside-jepa">Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latent forecasts need not expose contact or relative position. Inside-JEPA models entities and relations and studies how action supervision shapes them. A relation channel or low prediction loss does not establish learned relational semantics; controls are needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two unchanged-looking objects can transition from separated to touching, altering the right action despite unchanged categories.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与五臂. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31194-inside-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c81bf3ff739be368">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:inside-jepa" data-paper-title="Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-098a3adf3f209998">Why use a differentiable online future encoding in the inverse-dynamics head instead of EMA?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainside-jepa">Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The inverse objective must send action-explanation gradients into relationship representations on the future side. JEPA prediction can still use a stable EMA target. Entity-only and shuffled-action controls test whether relations truly supply action information.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict the action from changes in cup–box relations; the future relation encoder needs gradients to learn such changes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与五臂. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31194-inside-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-098a3adf3f209998">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:inside-jepa" data-paper-title="Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eec426b4717383d2">What do INV-S, INV-R, and shuffled-label controls isolate?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainside-jepa">Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>INV-S reads relations only for inverse dynamics; INV-R reads entity latents only. Shuffling changes only inverse labels, while prediction still reads true actions. These controls isolate supervision sources rather than treating any auxiliary gain as relation grounding.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar gains with random action labels suggest regularization rather than learned action–relation correspondence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与五臂. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31194-inside-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eec426b4717383d2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:inside-jepa" data-paper-title="Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-37cda28a2170cf1f">Why is the four-entity K=8 state 256-dimensional, not 224 after removing diagonals?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ainside-jepa">Inside-JEPA: From Prediction to Relational Grounding in Latent World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Australian Institute for Machine Learning, Adelaide University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Entity latents occupy 4×32 and ordered pair slots occupy 4×4×8. Padding and diagonals stay present but zero. JEPA uses detached EMA future targets; inverse dynamics needs differentiable online future state. Mixing them cuts a defining gradient.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Zeroing diagonal relationships does not delete their 32 slots or shrink the predictor interface.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与五臂, 本地复现与操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31194v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31194-inside-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-37cda28a2170cf1f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-jepa-prediction-planning-96c625cf" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c84d7475eab03391">Why does a small one-step JEPA latent loss not establish understanding of physical motion?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latents use encoder-specific coordinates; closeness need not mean accurate position, angle, speed, or long-horizon planning. This work checks physical decoding and actual planning separately, with shared training scales.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Similar latent vectors may decode to different object angles, so measure physical error and planning success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c84d7475eab03391">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c221d8dad06e5450">Why subtract decoding error on true next representations from decoding error on predicted ones?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Decoding error mixes encoder readability, decoder limitations, and prediction error. Using the same frozen decoder for both isolates excess error attributable to prediction more closely. It can be negative and must not be clipped. Long-horizon planning needs separate paired tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If real representations decode two cells off and predicted ones three cells off, do not attribute all three cells to prediction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c221d8dad06e5450">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dedb423059826135">Why measure one-step physical error and planning success separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A planner repeatedly queries the model; errors can accumulate around key actions or alter search. One-step means miss closed-loop effects. Test actual planning with paired seeds and the same checkpoint and task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Better accuracy on common stationary states can lower average error even if near-collision mistakes make plans crash.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dedb423059826135">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:jepa-prediction-planning" data-paper-title="One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cd7787052f6ef35f">Should negative E_excess be clipped to zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ajepa-prediction-planning">One-Step Prediction Fidelity Is a Poor Proxy for Planning Performance in JEPA World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It is decoded error from predictions minus decoded error from true representations; predictions may happen to fit the frozen decoder better. Identical representations must yield zero. Fit state variance on shared training data, never refit the decoder on predicted test latents.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>True error three and predicted error two gives −1; clipping hides decoder extrapolation behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 聚合、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19375v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.19375-jepa-prediction-planning/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cd7787052f6ef35f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lewam" data-paper-title="LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-lewam-7895d3a3" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1a6959f95b4f9227">Why link predicting consequences with producing usable actions in LeWAM training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alewam">LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A world model can predict an action&#x27;s future without finding goal-reaching actions efficiently. A separate policy may not shape visual representations. Joint state, dynamics, and stochastic action learning shares signals, but does not remove isolation or execution requirements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing a push moves an object is not the same as deciding which direction and distance to push.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12818">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1a6959f95b4f9227">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lewam" data-paper-title="LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-64e4dca51fbd2f0a">Why prevent LeWAM&#x27;s noisy-action branch from seeing clean actions indirectly?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alewam">LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clean actions supervise future dynamics for state queries but are unavailable to the deployed action policy. Indirect access through shared attention would let the noisy branch copy targets. Separate parameters alone do not prevent leakage; enforce visibility across layers.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A provided “push left” label can train prediction but must not be read by the action generator and counted as a decision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12818">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-64e4dca51fbd2f0a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
