<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lewam" data-paper-title="LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-7d7c630753bca65d">How does action flow differ from wide Gaussian random search?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alewam">LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Flow matching learns velocities from noise to action data, proposing candidates nearer the learned distribution before planning in latent dynamics. Wide Gaussian search relies on unstructured coverage. Actual task advantage requires controlled validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A learned proposal might favor plausible pushes along a table instead of many trajectories through it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12818">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7d7c630753bca65d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lewam" data-paper-title="LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c23e22f887512a09">Why refine actions with a proximity penalty but select by the original goal cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alewam">LeWAM: End-to-End World and Action Modeling with JEPAs</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · UC San Diego</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Adam penalizes deviations from the sampled plan to constrain refinement. Final selection compares unpenalized goal cost, retaining original samples in case refinement worsens them. Planning updates actions, not model weights, and does not guarantee real success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A refined action that deviates more can still win if it reaches the predicted goal more closely; keep the original if refinement fails.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 数据协议、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12818">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.12818-lewam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c23e22f887512a09">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-locale-jepa-ba12e8f4" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3d704fc3d2d42061">Why prevent collapse if two views of the same image should agree?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A constant vector also gives perfect view agreement. LocaLeJEPA wants invariance across augmentations and distinguishable representations across inputs while respecting local geometry. A low agreement loss does not establish useful features.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Cat crops should be close, but collapsing cats and cars together ruins retrieval.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3d704fc3d2d42061">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-039c7085ea195e93">Why not pull all LocaLeJEPA clusters toward one Gaussian?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local clusters have different geometries and positions. A global pull can destroy layout. Fix group assignments, recenter residuals per cluster, and match a uniform solid-ball distribution, with an explicit small-cluster fallback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two clusters for different motion modes can keep distinct centers while each has a regular local shape.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-039c7085ea195e93">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-cfaad9a651dc6033">How does a uniform solid ball differ from a Gaussian or a unit sphere surface?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The solid ball puts mass inside radius √(d+2), giving identity covariance. A Gaussian is unbounded and a sphere surface has mass at a fixed radius only. Their characteristic functions differ. Gaussian formulas or vector normalization cannot replace the target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A uniform disk includes points near its center; a circle does not, and a Gaussian extends to arbitrary radius.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cfaad9a651dc6033">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:locale-jepa" data-paper-title="LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c22e52ed3c5a5bb">How do small-cluster filtering and cluster count change regularization strength?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alocale-jepa">LocaLeJEPA: Maximum Entropy Representations under Geometric Priors</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Pennsylvania</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Keep clusters with at least four samples; fall back to the full batch and log it if none qualify. Multiply each cluster statistic by sample count, then average equally over valid clusters and views. Count changes both granularity and scale. Integrate the ball characteristic function, not a Gaussian target.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting into more valid small clusters changes the value through weighting and averaging even with the same λ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 验证与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28458v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.28458-locale-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c22e52ed3c5a5bb">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-mice-b52a199b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7fbd2b03fd6b9570">How does attribute leakage violate a multi-instance edit?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Different objects may need different changes, but unbound color, shape, or texture can spread to other objects. MICE maintains local assignments and contextual blending without new training. Success is applying each requested change only to the right instance, not just making a prettier image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Left cup red and right cup blue should not yield two purple cups.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7fbd2b03fd6b9570">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-17c3380975ca6c68">Why need both text-group isolation and smooth spatial bias for multi-instance editing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Text isolation stops one instruction directly modifying another group&#x27;s semantics. Smooth spatial bias binds edits to instances while blending at boundaries. Hard cuts can show seams; global text can leak color. This attention control does not train a new editor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep “left shoe red” and “right shoe blue” semantically separate while blending each localized edit naturally.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-17c3380975ca6c68">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-5967ac30be26b54d">How does smooth spatial bias differ from a hard mask outside the region?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Log-smoothed masks give finite negative bias that fades near boundaries; hard masks prohibit interactions. Unrelated text groups still use negative infinity, and pixels belonging to other instances are zeroed. Local behavior follows paper_v1, not every author default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Weak interactions near a shadow can aid blending while isolating another instance&#x27;s exclusive pixels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5967ac30be26b54d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:mice" data-paper-title="Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9dcf4741dcb5f179">Why use at least float32 for ε=10^-30 and avoid arbitrary context-to-vision masks?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Amice">Editing Everything Everywhere All at Once</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Modena and Reggio Emilia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>FP16 can underflow ε and turn finite log bias into −∞. Softmax and accumulation need at least FP32. The local implementation follows text Case 5: context sees the full visual domain without spatial bias, rather than mixing incompatible diagram or processor defaults.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Computing log(ε) after underflow changes intended soft decay into a hard exclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 原文与代码版本边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31278v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2606.31278-mice/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9dcf4741dcb5f179">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-oob-regularization-98328dd1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-24c359d6bb05f722">Why might a small-batch SSL model align views without learning distinguishable features?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Positive alignment alone allows a constant encoder. Anti-collapse needs overall spread, which small batches estimate poorly. OOB uses broader statistics under memory constraints, but downstream performance still needs independent evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Several similar embeddings may reflect genuinely similar images or global collapse; view agreement alone cannot tell.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-24c359d6bb05f722">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-39f15ae4c6df1bd0">How does OOB provide near-dataset-scale anti-collapse supervision with a small batch?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Periodically encode the training set and cache anchors per sample, then read fixed targets during small-batch optimization. This avoids estimating the full distribution every step but requires refresh as the model changes. It is not a minibatch variance or covariance loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If memory holds eight images, precompute full-training-set quantile targets and match each of those eight to its own anchor.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-39f15ae4c6df1bd0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-62e96fc660a402dc">How does Gaussian sorted-quantile matching differ from enforcing zero mean and unit variance?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sorted quantiles assign normal targets to samples along random projections, constraining distributions and assignments. Mean and variance constrain only two moments. This is not the original Epps–Pulley statistic; matched baselines need the same quantile loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal mass at −1 and +1 has mean zero and variance one but not normal quantiles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62e96fc660a402dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:oob-regularization" data-paper-title="Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5fcebfd43f84ed2a">How should refresh directions, targets, and gradients be isolated?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aoob-regularization">Dataset-Level Regularization for Joint-Embedding Self-Supervised Learning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Freeze refreshed directions and per-sample targets, detach them and store on CPU. Normalize online loss by batch B, views V, and directions M; no gradients through refresh. The spherical variant optimizes unit anchors, not Gaussian targets. Stable sample IDs are required.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>After dataloader shuffling, look up each original ID rather than pairing the first cached anchor with the first current image.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界与成本结论. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.20158">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.20158-oob-regularization/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5fcebfd43f84ed2a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ppmem-5417d641" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4111c1cac44a1ce5">Why do long video generators forget scene layout when returning to an old viewpoint?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A few recent frames omit earlier geometry; storing all pixels or points is costly. PPMem maintains compact rasterizable planes across chunks for revisits. Planes approximate scenes and still need occlusion/error management. Persistence alone is not consistency.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>When a camera returns to a desk, persistent memory can preserve a bookshelf that has been absent from recent frames.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与流程. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4111c1cac44a1ce5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ffec7e05ce43b92">Why is plane eviction using the next camera path not reading real future video?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The path can be a provided generation control: it says where the camera will point, not what real pixels will appear. The plane pool prepares for better observations, but the model must generate them. Unknown future observations or gold geometry would be leakage.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A specified orbit around a table tells where to look without revealing the texture on the back.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与流程. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ffec7e05ce43b92">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e1ace68dd5ef5979">How does a persistent plane pool differ from conditioning only on recent frames?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Recent context forgets distant views. A world-coordinate pool supplies geometry during revisits and requires occlusion voting, quality deduplication, and eviction. Known future camera pose does not supply real future video.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A room orbit can reuse an old wall while eviction knows the next camera location, not future pixels.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与流程. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e1ace68dd5ef5979">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppmem" data-paper-title="Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-873512f352f628c0">Is geometry LoRA enabled at every video denoising step?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appmem">Persistent Planar Memory for Video World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Denoise with the frozen stage-one backbone and geometry LoRA off. After generating video, run one extra geometry forward with LoRA to extract planes. Training also uses depth, normals, rasterization, and smoothing, with no rasterization loss in the first thousand steps. Local status is documentation only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generate a 25-frame chunk through multiple steps, then extract planes once and merge the pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与流程, 本地复现与成本判断. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23795">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23795-ppmem/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-873512f352f628c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-raw-video-midtraining-db4472b0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-176304cc6cc0aa4d">Why can uncaptioned video provide a useful language-model midtraining signal?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ordered frames contain objects, motion, and spatiotemporal relationships not fully captured by text. The method turns frame patches into continuous sequences and predicts future representations causally. This is not captioning or proof of physical understanding; test after matched tuning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Video of lifting a cup preserves motion that the caption “someone picks up a cup” may omit.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与原文效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-176304cc6cc0aa4d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-cca299426ddfa506">Why does target stop-gradient not freeze the entire vision tokenizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Detaching targets prevents them from moving or collapsing with predictions. The input-side tokenizer still receives gradients through the LM and prediction head. Caption-free midtraining learns visual sequence relations and needs matched instruction tuning for comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>The next patch is detached as target, but prediction error still updates the tokenizer through earlier input patches.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与原文效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cca299426ddfa506">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1aa77b19c09a3bc6">What supervision bottleneck does raw video avoid compared with captions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Captions capture only described information, often omitting continuous motion and detail. Continuous token prediction uses raw order but costs longer sequences and vision regression. Better semantics are not guaranteed; match subsequent instruction tuning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>“A ball moves” omits path and speed variation; raw video contains them, but downstream tests show whether the model uses them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与原文效果. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1aa77b19c09a3bc6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:raw-video-midtraining" data-paper-title="Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a155f198062cb83">Why match image-text instruction tuning after video midtraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Araw-video-midtraining">Mid-Training Language Models on Raw Video</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Meta AI / Massachusetts Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Final ability depends on both stages. Different later tuning would confound the raw-video effect. The paper matches later tuning, so text-retention conclusions apply to that protocol, not arbitrary captionless training. A local component is not the full comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Giving only the video arm extra high-quality instructions would confound a later visual QA gain.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与原文效果, 本地复现与成本决策. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11019">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.11019-raw-video-midtraining/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a155f198062cb83">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-smolwam-cc2de315" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0aa7cf4f31b523e5">Why lighten the entire video-generative robot interface in SmolWAM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Vision encoding, video backbone, text conditioning, and action representation all cost compute. A small action head alone can leave most costs. Each change needs compatibility checks and recovery training before real control validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tiny action head still pays for a large VAE, long visual input, and multistep denoising.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0aa7cf4f31b523e5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-6d581a20417b2084">Why preserve original token positions and rectified-flow direction when shrinking action queries?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The pretrained trunk expects particular position semantics and a data-to-noise velocity. A lighter interface that changes them adds distribution shift. SmolWAM restores compatibility stage by stage; checkpoint loading alone does not establish equivalent behavior.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reading teacher velocity noise-minus-data with an opposite-sign recovery rule can move actions the wrong way.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6d581a20417b2084">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9f6b8f26a0b0653d">How does a single-frame VAE plus adapter differ from directly replacing the VAE?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The teacher expects a video-clip latent distribution. The adapter maps single-frame outputs back into that space to preserve a usable trunk interface. Matching shape or token positions alone does not align numeric scale or spatiotemporal semantics.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two encoders can output identically shaped tensors but different distributions; the adapter learns compatibility.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9f6b8f26a0b0653d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smolwam" data-paper-title="SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-b896fba15c6b0841">Does SmolWAM use the same rectified-flow velocity direction as LeWAM?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmolwam">SmolWAM: A Latent World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation on Edge Devices</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · ML Collective</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. SmolWAM follows teacher data-to-noise interpolation xτ=(1−τ)x0+τε, with velocity ε−x0 and a consistent clean estimate. LeWAM uses the opposite direction. Retain the 12 specified blocks, original positions, and zero-bias sink rather than borrowing another formula.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Reversing velocity during recovery moves the action in the wrong direction even if loss code runs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 数据协议、结果与边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13740">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.13740-smolwam/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b896fba15c6b0841">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-time-jepa-c002ea0d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-4391c33e37078638">Why are action classes different from exact speeds or joint angles?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Classification can be invariant across speeds and poses, while control and physical analysis need continuous detail. Time-JEPA adds temporal physical supervision without using sensors at deployment. Correct labels cannot establish numeric precision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two clips can both show “raising a hand” with different speeds and elbow angles.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与隔离要求. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4391c33e37078638">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-045efa8d388d00cd">How can training-only physical time series improve a video-only encoder?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Auxiliary heads predict speed or joint angles from video and send gradients back to the encoder. Remove the head at deployment; sensor values never enter inputs. Mask invalid frames and fit normalization on training only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Train with synchronized speed labels and test on video alone. Supplying speed at test would change the task.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与隔离要求. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-045efa8d388d00cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bfed14e3e777d72b">What does physical supervision add beyond masked latent prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Latent prediction encourages predictability without ensuring precise physical variables survive. Synchronized labels directly encourage those variables in the encoder. Benefits depend on variable coverage and distribution; one domain&#x27;s probe does not establish universal physical or control ability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A model can predict road texture while ignoring speed differences until a speed target requires them.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与隔离要求. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bfed14e3e777d72b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:time-jepa" data-paper-title="Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-4693c64708e6cbb5">Can a fully missing variable in one tubelet be filled with a valid zero?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atime-jepa">Time-JEPA: Grounding Video World Models with Physical Time Series</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Harbin Institute of Technology</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Average valid frames independently per variable; empty tubelets remain invalid. Fit and freeze normalization on training. Apply SmoothL1 with β=0.5 only to valid entries, with domain-specific heads, statistics, and weights.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If neither frame has a joint-angle measurement, skip that variable instead of treating missing as a true zero angle.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式与隔离要求, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23982-time-jepa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4693c64708e6cbb5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-multimodal-models-uniaction-704ab058" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-22a1c4fa397b7c64">Why should action token count not directly represent importance across formats?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Equivalent actions can be tokenized at different granularity. UniAction separates element identity and position and corrects joint attention for count effects. Genuine added actions still carry new information; not every longer encoding is meaningless duplication.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Splitting a path into 20 rather than ten segments does not double importance, but adding a real grasp matters.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-22a1c4fa397b7c64">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-32b91700ff0ec00d">Why does adding log(Nref/Na) to action logits cancel identical action-token duplication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>In joint softmax, copying identical keys, values, and positions increases the action exponent sum. The log-count bias cancels that multiplicity while preserving relative action logits. Different new content or positions can still affect outputs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Duplicating each token with identical position would raise uncorrected action weight; corrected output should not change from count alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-32b91700ff0ec00d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-867e752facaab6ed">How does corrected joint softmax differ from separately normalizing video and action then summing?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint normalization shares one denominator and applies log(Nref/Na) to action logits. Separate softmax gives each stream total mass one before merging, a different cross-modal weighting even if internal action ranks match.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Strong video and weak action evidence can yield low total action weight jointly, but separate softmax forces a full action share.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-867e752facaab6ed">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="multimodal-models:uniaction" data-paper-title="UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="multimodal-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0438a167c0dd745e">Does duplication invariance allow arbitrary added actions or changed positions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=multimodal-models%3Auniaction">UniAction: Unified Action Conditioning for World Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Exact invariance requires identical key, value, and position representations. Na counts valid actions per request; padding is excluded and has zero attention. Supply the native position callback explicitly; local diagnostics are not Wan&#x27;s native position mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Copying the same action at another time changes position, so changed output does not violate invariance.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.32977v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../multimodal-models/2610.32977-uniaction/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0438a167c0dd745e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-vbvr-pro-eb931970" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-a689a1bd0391b575">Why can an attractive final image fail the visual reasoning task?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Rules may constrain motion, intermediate states, and forbidden areas. A correct-looking ending can hide process violations. VBVR-Pro turns known rules into executable checks, without measuring undefined quality or assuming every task has a reliable scorer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An object can reach its goal by crossing a forbidden area; only the trajectory check catches it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a689a1bd0391b575">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-3c05a2d2ce10e7f4">Why prefer an executable scorer to a general VLM judge for some spatiotemporal constraints?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Explicit intermediate states, constraints, and goals can be checked per example rather than by fluency. Executable rewards cover only defined rules. Scorer correctness, gold isolation, and actual trajectory generation still need separate checks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Verify each move avoids walls and reaches the target; a fluent explanation does not excuse crossing a wall.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3c05a2d2ce10e7f4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-f61addb2d17becd9">Is a weighted constraint reward equivalent to requiring all constraints to pass?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Weighted sums permit compensation; a hard conjunction makes any violation infeasible. Higher total reward does not guarantee every constraint. This compares objective semantics, not an additional author ablation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One of two equally weighted checks gives half credit, while a mandatory safety check cannot be offset by success elsewhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f61addb2d17becd9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vbvr-pro" data-paper-title="VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8bddbd7e921c7fde">What does the local programmatic reward&#x27;s gain over a noisy baseline to a perfect score show?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avbvr-pro">VBVR-Pro: A Scalable and Verifiable Suite for Native Visual Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University / VBVR Community</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It shows deterministic task scoring and failure attribution on the supplied programs are more stable than a noisy judge analogue. It does not show a multimodal generator gained ability after RLVR. Real trajectories, model updates, and independent evaluation are still needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scoring a known valid trajectory as one tests the scorer, not a generator&#x27;s ability to discover it.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.26105">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.26105-vbvr-pro/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8bddbd7e921c7fde">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-vjepa-policy-d720eedd" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5edd75f877906c0b">Why condition robot actions on what the model expects to see?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Current images alone may not indicate how the goal changes the scene. V-JEPA Policy connects instruction-conditioned prediction with action learning, giving the action expert predicted context. No future ground truth enters control, and actual execution must still be tested.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict the cup inside a box without reading an actual completion image before the robot moves.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37250">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5edd75f877906c0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b1dc62a377da6fe6">How does reading predicted future latents differ from reading actual future frames?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Predictions come from current observations and instructions and are available at deployment. Real future is training-only supervision. The action expert reads computable foresight, not actual outcomes. Frozen visual encoders do not prevent forecast errors from accumulating.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict a cup&#x27;s position after grasping; do not feed the real post-grasp photo before judging policy success.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37250">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.37250-vjepa-policy/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b1dc62a377da6fe6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-eae201df1d76d128">How does joint world/action training differ from separately training a predictor and action head?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Joint training coordinates future context and action flow so predictions can serve control needs. Independent stages need not align. The vision encoder stays frozen; joint predictor/action training does not update every visual parameter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Future grasp context can adapt to the action head while the V-JEPA encoder weights remain unchanged.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:vjepa-policy" data-paper-title="V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="multimodal-models" data-topic="multimodal-models/world-state-actions">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Multimodal models / Visual world models: state, generation, and action conditioning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-44f9ff0a4f6450b9">How are future-target gradients isolated, and what is locally implemented?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Avjepa-policy">V-JEPA Policy: Building Effective World-Action Models on Predictive Visual Latents</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Tsinghua University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Encode actual future with frozen vision and stop gradients. Apply masked L1 and train action velocity. Local work checks future-latent isolation and flow only; no V-JEPA 2.1 checkpoint or robot dataset. Three-seed small tensors do not validate a LIBERO policy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>No target gradient confirms supervision isolation, not robot success without rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
